input_signals.name: Cash-Versus-Book Distress Divergence in R&D Firms
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(xrd, sale)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), lt)), RANK(RATIO(re, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: For intangible-intensive firms, accrual-based distress metrics (retained earnings) and cash-based solvency (operating cash flow to liabilities) diverge systematically; the divergence, not the level, identifies firms whose distress is purely an artifact of accounting.
input_signals.reasoning: The bracketed term is positive when a firm looks weak on accumulated book earnings yet generates cash flow that comfortably services liabilities, which is the signature of expensed intangible investment. Scaling by R&D intensity concentrates the effect where the accounting bias originates rather than where earnings management or cyclicality drives the gap. High-divergence research firms should be repriced upward as cash flows validate solvency.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( xrd, sale ) ), sub( rank( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), lt ) ), rank( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Research Budget and Rollover Coverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(MA(oancf, 3), ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), dlc)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: For research-intensive firms, fragility is a flow-timing problem: recurring operating cash flow must simultaneously fund the ongoing research budget and retire debt maturing within the year, and firms failing that joint test must either cut innovation or refinance under duress.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the archived static stock measure (cash and cash flow against total liabilities) for a flow-based rollover test that nets the research commitment itself out of available cash flow, so the two proposals teach different lessons about whether the innovation premium is a cushion effect or a refinancing-risk effect. The conditional product is retained deliberately — the coverage test is only economically meaningful where a research budget exists — and coalescing R&D to zero keeps non-reporters in the sample at the bottom of the conditioning leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( ma( oancf, 3 ), add( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), dlc ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Research Runway Against Cash Burn
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(RATIO(che, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MA(oancf, 3)), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: For a research-intensive firm, survival is a duration question — how many years of the research program the existing cash stock can fund at the current burn rate — and firms with long runway can carry accounting losses indefinitely without genuine fragility.
input_signals.reasoning: Prior solvency legs compared resources to total liabilities, but liabilities are not what kills an innovator; the binding constraint is exhausting cash while research spending exceeds internal cash generation, which is a distinct economic clock. The rank difference between the cash cushion and the burn rate is bounded and defined for all firms, and multiplying by research intensity restricts the runway concept to firms where it is economically meaningful.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), sub( rank( ratio( che, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), ma( oancf, 3 ) ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pure Demeaned Research-Coverage Interaction
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), ZSCORE(SUB(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), at), RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Debt-service coverage should matter far more for the pricing of firms whose asset base is unverifiable knowledge capital than for firms with tangible collateral, so the priced object is the cross-product of the two centered attributes rather than either level.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive interaction multiplies two non-negative ranks, so the long leg mechanically contains high R&D intensity and the result cannot be distinguished from a known single-theme R&D effect; centering both legs removes their main effects and leaves only the interaction, which is what the task actually asks for. If this signal retains meaningful alpha, the conditional mechanism is real; if it vanishes, the archive's alphas are a repackaged R&D-intensity premium and the search should pivot decisively to the goodwill/impairment short leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), zscore( sub( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), at ), ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Research Floor Under Peak Indebtedness
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that never let its research intensity fall below a high floor even in the year its indebtedness peaked has demonstrated, through revealed behaviour, that its financing constraint was not binding; that demonstrated resilience distinguishes accounting distress from genuine fragility better than any contemporaneous ratio.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the balance-sheet-repair family entirely for a revealed-preference mechanism: the floor of research intensity over three years versus the peak of leverage over the same window, so the long leg contains firms that funded innovation *through* their worst debt year rather than firms that simply look adjusted-solvent today. The failed gen-0 retrenchment signal used noisy one-year growth rates in both legs, whereas floors and peaks are stable order statistics of levels, and coalescing R&D to zero keeps non-reporters at the bottom of the commitment leg rather than dropping them.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_min( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_max( ratio( lt, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Organic Share of Soft Capital Under Net Debt Strain
input_signals.expression: MUL(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dltt, dlc), che), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among strained firms holding soft capital, the fraction of that capital which was internally generated rather than purchased determines whether the strain is an artifact: organic knowledge capital is understated on the books and generates cash, whereas goodwill is already capitalized and generates none.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual-like earnings-minus-cash-flow leg is removed entirely, so the result cannot be a rediscovery of the Sloan effect; the conditioner is instead net interest-bearing debt over assets, a pure balance-sheet strain measure. The composition leg is also rebuilt as a bounded [0,1] share of soft capital rather than a difference of two independently ranked intensities, which makes it a coherent single quantity, immune to the scale mismatch between a five-year expense flow and a balance-sheet stock, and defined only for firms that actually hold intangible capital of some kind.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), add( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( dltt, dlc ), che ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Revenue Servicing Capacity of Research Firms
input_signals.hypothesis: Revenue, not cash flow or profit, is the least manipulable evidence that a research firm's knowledge capital has reached commercial scale, and a large revenue base relative to obligations means the firm can refinance or grow into its liabilities regardless of what its earnings look like.
input_signals.reasoning: Every conditioner tested so far is a cash-flow, cash-stock or balance-sheet quantity, all of which are affected by the same accounting conventions that create the false-distress problem; revenue-to-liabilities is a commercial-scale measure that is immune to expensing, impairment and accrual choices. It also discriminates within the R&D-intensive population between pre-revenue firms, where the distress label may be genuine, and commercialized innovators, where it is an artifact — a distinction none of the archived signals makes.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sale, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Lending Beyond Pledgeable Collateral
input_signals.hypothesis: Term lenders extend credit against tangible collateral by default, so a research-intensive firm carrying long-term debt far in excess of its tangible asset base has been underwritten on the strength of knowledge assets that lenders verified and the balance sheet omits.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a stock-based collateral-adequacy measure rather than the archived one-year financing flow, and the scaling by tangible assets is the point: it identifies borrowing that could only have been approved on unrecorded asset value, which is the certification mechanism the flow signal could only hint at. The economics are testable and distinct — the same excess of debt over collateral is unambiguously bad for a firm without knowledge capital, so the intangible gate is doing real conditioning work rather than re-signing an archived product.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( dltt, sub( at, coalesce( intan, 0 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Growing Into Obligations
input_signals.hypothesis: An innovator whose revenue base is expanding faster than its obligations is deleveraging through commercialization, so its current distress ratios are a snapshot of a rapidly improving position rather than a stable state.
input_signals.reasoning: Rather than re-scaling the same static commercial-scale numerator, this changes the economic object from level to *relative rate*: the race between revenue and liabilities, which is what determines whether today's leverage will still bind next year. It is also immune to the gross-profitability rediscovery concern because neither leg is a profitability measure, and the difference of two growth rates is centred near zero rather than inheriting the level of either.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( sub( growth( sale, 1 ), growth( lt, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunction of Leverage and Cash Coverage
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), lt))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The mispriced population is the conjunction — research firms that are simultaneously heavily obligated and comfortably servicing those obligations from operations — because that is exactly the group a leverage-based screen flags and a cash-flow test exonerates.
input_signals.reasoning: The rank sum genuinely failed to compute the stated hypothesis, since it scores a safe unlevered firm identically to a strained one; taking the minimum of the two rank legs makes the conditioner high only when *both* conditions hold, which is the correct operator for a conjunction and is untested in this archive. This also removes the objection that the signal loads positively on raw leverage: leverage alone now contributes nothing, because a high-leverage firm with weak coverage is floored by its coverage rank.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), min( rank( ratio( lt, at ) ), rank( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Multi-Year Coverage Trajectory of Innovators
input_signals.hypothesis: For research firms the relevant solvency information is the direction the coverage ratio has been travelling for years, not its level in a single year, because a sustained upward trajectory is evidence that the knowledge capital is progressively converting into debt-servicing capacity.
input_signals.reasoning: The one-year change version earned a 0.039 alpha at t=3.09 but only a 1.29 slope, consistent with a genuine effect measured with too much noise; a five-year fitted trend is a far more precise estimate of the same state variable and is the one temporal construction the archive has never used. Because a trend is centred near zero and roughly symmetric, it should also produce the dispersed, monotone conditioner that the strong-slope signals share.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ), rank( trend( ratio( oancf, lt ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Brand Capital Servicing Capacity
input_signals.hypothesis: If the false-distress mechanism is really about expensed intangible investment rather than about R&D-intensive industries, then accumulated advertising — the other major expensed intangible — should show the same premium when paired with commercial scale relative to obligations.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's best joint result rests entirely on R&D, and the failed gross-margin experiments left open whether the effect is an intangible-accounting phenomenon or a research-industry phenomenon; substituting advertising capital for research capital in the exact winning structure is the decisive external-validity test. A positive result would broaden the mechanism to consumer and media firms and materially strengthen the economic interpretation, while a null would justify concentrating the final generation exclusively on research capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xad, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sale, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Acquired Equity Without Earned Profits
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm whose asset base is largely purchased goodwill while its accumulated retained earnings are thin or negative has never demonstrated that it can generate profit internally; its apparent scale was bought with external capital, so its solvency rests entirely on an intangible that cannot be recovered.
input_signals.reasoning: Both legs are stock levels rather than one-year changes, so the signal cannot be a restatement of the asset-growth or net-debt-issuance anomalies that contaminated the acquisition-event version. The pairing of goodwill intensity with the accumulated-earnings channel is untested in the archive — every prior goodwill signal used leverage, cash-flow or revenue conditioners — and it isolates the specific genuine-fragility case the theme requires: soft capital that was bought rather than built, held by a firm with no internal profit history to fall back on.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Economic Net Worth per Dollar of Obligations
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm's true equity backing for its obligations is what it has earned and retained, plus what it has invested in research and expensed, minus what it paid above fair value in acquisitions; that single quantity is the complete restatement the false-distress story requires.
input_signals.reasoning: This unites the archive's best portfolio leg with its strongest correctly-signed slope channel — accumulated retained earnings, which produced −3.26 when crossed with goodwill — into one coherent economic quantity rather than a product of ranked legs. Because all three components are equity-like and enter additively in dollars before scaling, the construction is dimensionally consistent and avoids the mismatched-denominator problem that has weakened earlier composites.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), lt ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Goodwill Claimed Beyond Cash Realized
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill is the capitalized promise of future cash flows from an acquisition; when a firm's goodwill intensity ranks far above its actual cash-generating intensity, the promise has not been realized and the carrying value is an impairment waiting to happen.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the retained-earnings leg — itself a documented distress-quality anomaly with the same sign — with the operating cash flow the acquired assets were supposed to produce, so the signal measures corroboration of an accounting claim rather than restating a known quality metric. The bounded rank difference keeps both tails informative and defined for all firms, and it directly implements the run's central asymmetry: organic capital is understated and must be added back, acquired capital is overstated and must be validated against cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ), rank( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Economic Net Worth Against Financial Debt
input_signals.expression: RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)))
input_signals.hypothesis: True equity backing — earned and retained profits plus expensed research minus purchased goodwill — should be measured against the obligations that can actually force default, namely interest-bearing debt net of the cash already available to retire it.
input_signals.reasoning: The two frontier signals differ in exactly one place each: the numerator that produced the archive's best slope (4.60) was scaled by total liabilities, while the denominator that produced the best alpha (0.067) was paired with a sparser numerator; crossing them is the single highest-value test remaining because the deficiencies are complementary rather than overlapping. The retained-earnings term populates the numerator for the majority of firms that report no research, eliminating the tie mass that flattens the champion's slope, while the financial-debt denominator preserves the tail separation that generates the alpha.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( ratio( sub( add( re, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), max( add( dltt, dlc ), che ) ) )

input_signals.name: Hidden Backing With Cash-Coverage Tiebreak
input_signals.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che)), RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), lt))
input_signals.hypothesis: Hidden asset backing determines which firms are misclassified, but for the majority of firms that hold neither research capital nor goodwill the measure is silent, and among those firms demonstrated cash servicing capacity is what separates real from apparent distress.
input_signals.reasoning: The champion's flat slope is a construction problem with a specific cause — a numerator of exactly zero for the large block of firms reporting no R&D and no goodwill, which produces a tie mass that no linear regression can exploit — and adding a second ranked channel that is defined for every firm resolves those ties without disturbing the ordering at the informative extremes. Unlike the earlier three-channel additive score, neither component here is a standalone intangible-intensity measure: the first is a cross-theme backing ratio and the second a cash-coverage ratio, so the composite retains cross-theme content throughout its range.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sumrank( ratio( sub( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ), max( add( dltt, dlc ), che ) ), ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), lt ) )

input_signals.name: Conjunction of Hidden Backing and Cash-Corroborated Acquisitions
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), MAX(ADD(dltt, dlc), che))), RANK(SUB(RATIO(MA(oancf, 3), at), RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm qualifies as falsely distressed only if both conditions hold — it owns unrecorded research capital large relative to its debt, and whatever it did acquire is corroborated by the cash its operations actually produce — and failing either condition disqualifies it.
input_signals.reasoning: The additive ensemble was correctly criticised for penalising goodwill twice and for carrying a standalone profitability rank; here goodwill appears exactly once, inside a cross-theme difference against operating cash flow, and research appears exactly once, in the debt-scaled backing leg. The strict conjunction means neither channel can substitute for the other, which is a materially stronger and non-linear claim than any sum of the two archived components and cannot be replicated by reweighting them.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), max( add( dltt, dlc ), che ) ) ), rank( sub( ratio( ma( oancf, 3 ), at ), ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ) ) ) )
